review_type: source-grounded AI review; not physician adjudication
reviewed_components: all clinical facts and measured quantities
corrections: Heparin prophylaxis ("administered to the patients") and early-mobilization encouragement ("Patients were encouraged") lack an all-patients quantifier: made review_only (ambiguous) for p1-p4; their events set to occurrence unknown.

Melanoma resection facts keep only the explicit four-patient sentence and the Table 1 site; "The melanomas were fully resected" (abstract wide margins, Results appropriate margins) moved to a new review_only fact per patient.
Removed the "first reconstructive option ... for these patients" indication and quote from the four reconstruction facts (no all-patients quantifier); recorded as an ambiguity.
No major complications for Cases 2-4 made review_only: the sentence is series level and the Table 1 dashes have no legend.

Added a tumor board decision event per patient and relations: resection before reconstruction (Objective: defects after melanoma resection; Case 2 also the Secondary cell), sentinel node biopsy before tumor board decision (based on posterior sentinel node status), reconstruction before limb-function recovery (after a minimal 5-year follow-up).
Rewrote treatment and outcome summary claims to drop review-only content; updated domain coverage, source coverage notes, ambiguities and article limitations.
unresolved: Cohort level statements are not copied to individual patients unless the sentence explicitly covers all four patients or all cases: mean age, the sex split of three females and one male, the mean skin paddle size and range, the mean surgical time and range, and the count of patients with a vascular risk factor.
Series level outcome statements that name the series rather than the patients (100% flap survival, no partial flap necrosis, major complications not observed) are not copied to individual patients.
Sex is not documented for any individual patient: the text gives only counts (three females and one male) and Table 1 has no sex row, so no documented sex fact is recorded.

Operative Technique sentences without an all-patients quantifier (general anesthesia and margin protocol, in situ margin protocol, pivot point marking and intraoperative decision, tunneled or rotated pedicle, sentinel node biopsy technique with tracer and dye, 20-degree leg elevation, no pressure on the flap until the fourth postoperative week) describe the series and are not copied to individuals.
Counts without a named patient are not assigned to any patient: one tunneled pedicle (Fig. 5) with the rest rotated, and two patients who needed flap debulking 4 weeks after flap transposition.
The surgical indication criteria and the dermatology visit sentence in Methods describe patients who met the surgical indications and are not recorded as facts of each patient.

Source discrepancies recorded as ambiguities, not conflicts: the stated mean age of 54 years versus the Table 1 ages; three patients with a vascular risk factor versus a comorbidity for all four cases; three donor defects closed primarily and one skin graft versus two primary closures, one secondary closure and one skin graft.
The unit printed for the skin paddle sizes in the Results is cm with a superscript 3; these cohort statistics are not recorded.

Discussion and Conclusions are literature and author opinion; the sentence that heel numbness has not been a problem in our patients evaluates the series, and the sentence that no lesions have been documented due to the numbness names no subject, so neither is recorded as a patient fact.
All six figures are single photographs whose captions name no case, so figure ownership is unresolved; pixels are described in visual.json only.
The source lists no supplementary files.

Parent review: sentences about "the patients", "Patients", "The melanomas" or "these patients" without an all-patients quantifier (heparin prophylaxis, early mobilization, full resection, first reconstructive option) are not accepted per-patient facts; they are review only or recorded as ambiguities.

Table 1 prints dashes in the Complications row for Cases 2 to 4 without a legend, and the text statement of no major complications except patient number one is series level, so no major complications is review only for Cases 2 to 4. The Clark cell of Case 2 is blank and is not recorded.
Patient number one in the text is matched to Table 1 Case 1 by the same ordinal label, corroborated by the cellulitis and inguinal dissection cells.

key_findings: Every Table 1 cell checked against Cases 1-4 (age, comorbidities incl. the <break/>-split Case 3 cell, site, Breslow, Clark incl. blank Case 2 cell, margin, timing of reconstruction, donor closure, sentinel node, inguinal dissection, complications, follow-up, recurrence/metastasis); all correct.
Sex is given only as cohort counts (three females, one male); no per-patient sex fact is supportable. Age row has no time point: age_other kept.
Patient number one matched to Case 1 by the same ordinal label, corroborated by the cellulitis and dissection cells.
Mean age 54 vs Table ages (mean 52.5), 3 vs 4 risk-factor patients and 3 primary donor closures vs 2 primary + 1 secondary are arithmetic/count mismatches kept as ambiguities, not conflicts.
All six figure captions name no case; attribution stays unresolved.
residual_risks: Reading "the patients"/"The melanomas" in a 4-patient series as not explicitly covering all four is a strict reading of the cohort-copy rule.
Review-only by elimination: foot defect sites, Case 2 4-week secondary reconstruction, Case 4 2 x 3 cm graft.
Oral antibiotics clause may attach to the cellulitis or to the dissection; indication left unrecorded.
